sources.citation: Shpitser & Tchetgen Tchetgen, Annals of Statistics 2016

findings.finding: Path-specific effects are responses to edge/path intervention semantics and have stronger identification requirements than ordinary node interventions. A controlled dynamic node/state-cut effect does not by itself identify mediation through a causal path.
findings.impact: Keep H7 FORMAL-R1 PASS language, if any, at the frozen controlled dynamic TOP1 policy effect / panel distinctness claim. Do not paraphrase it as a route/path-mediated effect without a fresh separately identified path/edge intervention object.

sources.citation: Shpitser, identification review; Avin et al. / recanting criterion

findings.finding: When an intermediate variable or hidden district is required to carry conflicting treatment assignments along included and excluded paths, the path-specific counterfactual is not identified; this is the recanting-witness/district obstruction.
findings.impact: Recurrent/bypass/feedback H7 successors that claim effect transmission through a particular route should prospectively bind an edge/path graph and no-recanting/edge-consistency criterion or a physically separable intervention construction. The current total controlled cut effect remains well-defined.

sources.citation: Non-agency interventions for causal mediation, JRSS B 2024

findings.finding: Randomized interventional indirect effects can avoid some cross-world assumptions but need not satisfy a sharp mediational-null criterion; they may be nonzero even when no individual has an indirect mediated effect.
findings.impact: A future stochastic route intervention should remain an intervention-policy estimand unless sharper mechanistic mediation conditions are separately justified.

sources.citation: Vo et al., Statistics in Medicine 2026

findings.finding: Recanting-twin methods address intermediate confounding and include a falsification procedure for compatibility with intermediate confounding, providing a contemporary route to sharper path-specific analysis under stronger causal-model access.
findings.impact: Useful only as a future fresh stronger-privilege diagnostic ceiling where simulator/SCM variables are available; it must not be retrofitted into current FORMAL-R1 or used to choose its margins/interventions.

novelty_or_reduction_impact: PATH_SPECIFIC_MEDIATION_CLAIM_CEILING_SHARPENED_NO_CURRENT_FORMAL_CONTRACT_REWRITE. Stronger route-transmission claims require separately identified edge/path intervention semantics and no-recanting/separability conditions.
